inputs.text: Photorealistic Thai food photography for a Bangkok restaurant menu: a Thai-style creamy coconut curry, glossy and appetizing, with large visible cooked ingredients on top, served over jasmine rice on the SAME plate with plenty of rice grains exposed along one edge. Overhead close-up of ONE coherent finished Thai-inspired dish in ONE shallow blue-and-white Thai ceramic plate, on a warm teak table with a subtle banana-leaf placemat underneath the plate. The dish contains 6 selected ingredient types: Rice, Egg, Shrimp, Garlic, Mushroom, Coconut milk. All selected ingredients are large, individually recognizable and fully visible INSIDE the same plated dish: Thai jasmine rice with clearly visible individual grains; large pieces of Thai-style crispy fried egg with visible yellow yolk and white egg white; whole peeled cooked pink curled shrimp with recognizable tails; several peeled ivory garlic cloves with golden seared patches, each a plump curved pointed clove, no papery skins and no round bulbs; glossy pan-fried brown mushroom halves with dark seared surfaces, recognizable caps and stems; a visible glossy creamy coconut-milk sauce coating the dish, with pale ivory coconut-cream swirls clearly visible between the other ingredients. Distribute all selected ingredients visibly across the surface of this ONE cooked dish, integrated naturally with the Thai preparation while keeping every ingredient easy to recognize and uncovered. No isolated piles of ingredient samples, no compartment tray, no Western steak-and-sides plating. Every selected ingredient must be visible, not minced, pureed, buried or dissolved. Use only the selected visible food ingredients; do not add unselected rice, chili, basil, lime or other food garnishes. No separate ingredient bowls, raw ingredient display, collage, grid, labels, writing or hands. The food fills most of the frame. Warm natural daylight, realistic moist food textures, rich natural colors, sharp focus across the entire dish.
